note: Attacker-controlled raw CDP frame enters the decoder; pos/length delimit the readable window of the input buffer.
The number of address subframes in the CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES TLV is taken from the frame; each iteration parses one subframe.
Claimed address length of the current subframe is read (big-endian u16); addresses_len is decremented by the 2 header bytes only.
Bounds check against the remaining TLV bytes; it passes for the forged trailing subframe because addresses_len is overcounted (see step 5).

ROOT CAUSE: after skipping the claimed address bytes, addresses_len is NOT decremented by address_len (upstream fix a9aeabdf adds 'addresses_len -= address_len;'). The remaining-byte counter overcounts, so subsequent subframe bounds checks are defeated.
Position is rewound to the start of the subframe to re-parse it for IPv4 extraction, regardless of the overcounted length state.
Second pass: the forged trailing subframe (type=1, proto_len=1, proto=0xcc, addr_len=4) matches the IPv4 format test, so the 4-byte address read is attempted although no address bytes remain.
SINK: 4-byte memcpy read starting exactly at the end of the input buffer -> heap-buffer-overflow READ of 4 bytes (ASan) in the daemon while parsing CDP addresses.
